title: Evaluation scenario
description: One evaluation scenario, as docs/specs/skill-evaluation.md defines it: a mock project, the skills each condition installs, the git history the workspace starts from, the non-skill harness, the task the model is asked to perform, and the factors the result is judged on. This schema is the single declaration of that shape — tools/evaluation/src/scenario.mjs evaluates it rather than restating it. Its one rule that is not here is factor-id uniqueness, which standard JSON Schema cannot express; scenario.mjs checks that immediately afterward and says so.

id.description: "id" must be a non-empty string, equal to the name of the directory holding this scenario.

description.description: "description" must be a non-empty string stating what this scenario measures and why — a rationale a reader can disagree with without reading its factors.

mock.description: "mock" must be a non-empty string naming a directory under tools/evaluation/mocks/, which is what a probe's workspace is materialized from.

targetSkills.description: "targetSkills" must be a non-empty array of skill names. These are the skills under measurement: the skill-present condition installs them alongside peerSkills, and the skill-absent condition installs peerSkills alone.

peerSkills.description: "peerSkills" must be an array of skill names (may be empty). Both conditions install them, so a discovery factor asks a real question rather than a formality.

patch.description: "patch" must be present, and either null or a path to a unified diff. The path resolves against this scenario's own directory, and mock-workspace.mjs applies the diff after the mock is copied and before its history is replayed.

agentsMd.description: "harness.agentsMd" must be a boolean, saying whether the mock's own AGENTS.md is meant to reach the probe.

harness.description: "harness" must be an object declaring the non-skill harness the probe runs under.

prompt.description: "task.prompt" must be a string stating the problem in the words of whoever has it — naming neither the target skill, nor the mechanism that answers it, nor the defect's cause.

task.description: "task" must be an object carrying the task the probe is asked to perform.

factors.description: "factors" must be a non-empty array of what the result is judged on. Each factor's id must also be unique within the scenario — a rule this schema cannot express, checked separately by scenario.mjs.

nonBudgetKey.description: looks like a budget, a cost ceiling, or a dollar figure — a scenario declares no such thing (docs/specs/skill-evaluation.md; the admission bound this instrument enforces is a probe count, never a cost).
nonBudgetKey.$comment: refuses a key with a word starting budget, cost, dollar, price, or spend, or a word exactly cap, caps, capped, capping, or usd — words break on camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and capital runs. two boundaries are disclosed, not closed: costume is refused, an accepted false positive, since refusing an unrelated key is safer than admitting a real one; unpriced is admitted, since its price is not word-initial and reaching it would need the substring matching that produced the capUsd gap.

skillName.$comment: the name of a skill, as its own directory is named. deliberately carries no description: it is a shared value shape, and the field referencing it is what an author needs named.

scenarioRelativePath.$comment: a non-empty path relative to the scenario's own directory. deliberately carries no description, for the same reason as skillName.

id.description: a factor's "id" must be a non-empty string, unique within its scenario.

phase.description: a factor's "phase" must be one of discovery, outcome, transcript — which is what bounds the material its judge is shown.

description.description: a factor's "description" must be a non-empty string stating what this factor expects and why — a rationale a reader can disagree with without reading the judgment script.

factor.description: a factor must be an object declaring one thing the result is judged on.

method.description: a judgment's "method" must be one of script, reasoning.

judgment.description: how a factor is judged: a deterministic script run against the reconstructed workspace, or a reasoning judge asked to read the transcript.

script.description: a script judgment's "script" must name a module relative to the scenario's own directory.

scriptJudgment.description: a script judgment reads "script" and "input" and nothing else — a "model" or "instructions" here belongs to a reasoning judgment.

model.description: a reasoning judgment's "model" must be a vendor-prefixed, fully-qualified model id.

instructions.description: a reasoning judgment's "instructions" must be a non-empty string stating what the judge is asked to decide.

reasoningJudgment.description: a reasoning judgment reads "model" and "instructions" and nothing else — a "script" or "input" here belongs to a script judgment.

input.description: the arguments the named script is given, so one script can serve many factors. The instrument does not read inside it — factor-judgment.mjs copies it verbatim into the context file the script is handed, typed unknown in its own signature — and each script validates its own arguments, exiting non-zero with a reason when one is missing or malformed. This schema therefore says nothing about what shape an argument takes: that is the script's own contract, checked where it is used. The one rule it does carry inward is the repository's own, which no script checks — no key here, at any depth, may name a budget.

inputValue.description: any JSON value. Recursive for one reason only: so the no-budget rule reaches a key nested at any depth, which is the only thing this schema has to say about a script's arguments.
